W1.evidence: Removed `iterator` method in favour of [ES2015 iterator protocol](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Iterators_and_Generators ) which natively supports arrays

W3.evidence: Internal `setImmediate` calls have been refactored away.

W4.evidence: `map` used to return an object when iterating over an object.  `map` now always returns an array, like in other libraries.

W5.evidence: Any code that used to interact with this array will need to be updated to either use the provided helpers or support DLLs

W6.evidence: Calling a callback more than once is considered an error, and an error will be thrown.; `auto` task functions now always take the callback as the last argument.

W8.evidence: - `filter`, `reject`, `some`, `every`, and related functions now expect an error as the first callback argument, rather than just a simple boolean. Pass `null` as the first argument, or use `fs.access` instead of `fs.exists`. ([#118](https://github.com/caolan/async/issues/118), [#774](https://github.com/caolan/async/issues/774), [#1028](https://github.com/caolan/async/issues/1028), [#1041](https://github.com/caolan/async/issues/1041))

H1-a.evidence: To migrate old task functions, wrap them with [`_.flip`](https://lodash.com/docs#flip)

Y1.evidence: Another one of the general themes of the 2.0 release is standardization of what an "async" function is. We are now more strictly following the node-style continuation passing style.

W7-a.evidence: Async is also available as a collection of ES2015 modules in the new `async-es` package.
